Architecture Diagram

The application is a server-rendered catalog management site built with ASP.NET Web Forms on .NET Framework 4.7.2. Its catalog service can use either an in-memory mock or Entity Framework 6 backed by SQL Server LocalDB.

Data Storage & External Services

The configured database is SQL Server LocalDB, with Entity Framework mapping catalog items, brands, and types. When UseMockData is enabled, catalog operations instead use an in-memory mock service; the application also includes Application Insights instrumentation. No remote service endpoint is configured in the inspected application settings.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • ASP.NET Web Forms pages access catalog operations through the ICatalogService abstraction.
  • Autofac selects an in-memory mock or Entity Framework-backed service using the UseMockData setting.
  • Entity Framework 6 maps catalog items, brands, and types through CatalogDBContext.

DTOs & Contracts

The page/service contract is in-process and uses CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType as mutable domain model classes. PaginatedItemsViewModel represents the paginated catalog response model. Create and edit postback values are read from Web Forms controls and assembled into CatalogItem; no separate immutable request or response DTOs, OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, protobuf schemas, or GraphQL schemas were found. JSON serialization is not part of the observed page contract.

Communication Patterns

Browser communication is synchronous HTTP page rendering and Web Forms postback. Pages call ICatalogService directly; the selected implementation either uses Entity Framework synchronously or returns data from the in-memory mock service. There are no inter-service calls, message brokers, asynchronous communication patterns, API gateway, service discovery, load balancing, retries, circuit breakers, or configured timeout policies identified.

No API-level authentication, authorization, or TLS configuration was identified in the inspected application configuration; the application does not show endpoint role checks or a security middleware setup.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports maintaining a product catalog for an online shop, including browsing, classifying, and editing catalog items. Catalog data is managed within one application boundary; no cross-service business workflows were identified.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemeShopLegacyWebForms / Catalog ManagementA product offered in the shop, with pricing, stock, and catalog presentation informationBelongs to one catalog brand and one catalog type
CatalogBrandeShopLegacyWebForms / Catalog ManagementGroups products under a brandAssociated with catalog items
CatalogTypeeShopLegacyWebForms / Catalog ManagementClassifies products by typeAssociated with catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebFormsCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server LocalDB when database mode is selected; otherwise an in-memory mock catalog

All domain state is managed within the same application. No independently deployed service or cross-context data exchange was identified.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Create a Catalog Item

  1. A user opens the catalog item creation page and the application loads the available brands and types.
  2. The user submits the form. The page checks ModelState.IsValid; invalid submissions remain on the form without persisting an item.
  3. For a valid submission, the page creates a CatalogItem from the form and calls the catalog service.
  4. The service assigns an identifier and stores the new item through the selected data implementation.
  5. On success, the page redirects to the catalog landing page.

Workflow 2: Update or Remove a Catalog Item

  1. The user selects an existing item; the application loads it by route identifier and displays its details or edit/delete page.
  2. An edit submission is accepted only when ModelState.IsValid; the catalog service updates the item. A delete confirmation removes the selected item.
  3. Successful updates and removals redirect to the catalog landing page.

Workflow 3: Initialize Catalog Data

  1. At application startup, database initialization is configured only when mock data is disabled.
  2. When a new database is created, the initializer creates sequence objects and seeds catalog types, brands, and items.
  3. Seed records come from predefined data by default; optional customization files are used when customization data is enabled.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service data composition or aggregation pattern was found. Catalog item, brand, and type data are read and written within the same application; in mock mode, the in-memory service supplies catalog operations instead of the database-backed implementation. No remote-service fallback behavior is configured.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Catalog Manager" participant Page as "Catalog Create Page" participant Service as "Catalog Service" participant Store as "Catalog Store" User->>Page: Open item creation form Page->>Service: Load catalog brands and types Service->>Store: Read reference data Store-->>Service: Brands and types Service-->>Page: Reference data Page-->>User: Display creation form User->>Page: Submit catalog item alt Form validation succeeds Page->>Service: Create catalog item Service->>Store: Assign identifier and save item Store-->>Service: Save completed Service-->>Page: Item created Page-->>User: Redirect to catalog else Form validation fails Page-->>User: Redisplay form with validation state end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog changes are persisted only when the page model state is valid.
  • Price input must be a non-negative value with no more than two decimal places and within the configured maximum range.
  • Stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock values are constrained to the configured range from zero to ten million.
  • Catalog items require associated brand and type records in database mode.
  • Item identifiers are assigned by the catalog ID generator for newly created database-backed records.
  • UseMockData selects whether catalog operations use the mock or database-backed implementation; database initialization is only configured for database mode.
  • Database initialization seeds types and brands before catalog items so that the item references can be resolved.
  • Entity Framework SaveChanges persists individual mutations; no broader transaction orchestration, compensation, audit trail, or role-based authorization rule was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy ASP.NET Web Forms, Entity Framework 6.2.0, and older UI and telemetry packages. These dependencies require compatibility review for modernization; the existing Web Forms application model is tied to .NET Framework, and moving to a newer .NET runtime is not a simple target-framework change.

Notable Observations

  • NuGet dependencies are managed through the legacy packages.config format rather than SDK-style project package references.
  • The package inventory includes numerous .NET Framework support libraries and a compiler package, increasing the migration surface.
  • No security-specific package or dedicated caching, messaging, or test framework dependency is declared.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The data model contains three catalog entities persisted through Entity Framework 6 to SQL Server LocalDB when the application is configured for database-backed operation. A mock-data mode uses an in-memory catalog service instead.

Database Configuration

Service/ModuleDB TypeProfileDriverConnectionMigration Tool
eShopLegacyWebFormsSQL Server LocalDBMock data disabledSystem.Data.SqlClientLocalDB with integrated Windows authentication; no explicit connection-pool settings identifiedNo migration tool identified; database creation and seed initialization use Entity Framework
eShopLegacyWebFormsIn-memory mock dataMock data enabled (configured default)Not applicableProcess memoryNot applicable

When database initialization is enabled, CatalogDBInitializer creates a database if it does not exist, executes SQL sequence scripts, and seeds catalog types, brands, and items. Seed data comes from preconfigured code data or optional customization files. No schema-versioned migration framework was found.

Entity Model

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "categorizes" CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type } CatalogItem { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogTypeId FK int CatalogBrandId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder }

CatalogItem is persisted as the Catalog table, with foreign keys to CatalogBrand and CatalogType. The EF relationship is unidirectional from the item to its brand and type; each item requires one of each. PictureUri is a non-persisted property. Entity definitions are in src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogItem.cs, CatalogBrand.cs, and CatalogType.cs; the mappings are in src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogDBContext.cs.

No separate repository classes, custom repository query annotations, or explicit transaction-scope configuration were identified. Entity Framework SaveChanges is used for individual mutations.

Caching Strategy

No caching provider or cache policy was identified. The in-memory mock service is an alternate data implementation, not a cache for the database-backed service. ASP.NET session state is configured in-process but is not used as a catalog cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog data is owned by the single Web Forms application and stored in one SQL Server LocalDB database in non-mock mode; no cross-service database access or service-level data separation was found. The CatalogService accesses data directly through CatalogDBContext and performs synchronous reads and writes. The mock-data configuration substitutes an in-memory catalog implementation. No CQRS or cross-service aggregation pattern was identified.
